newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC June profit down.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC June profit down.

text.p: Taiwan state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Tuesday its June pre-tax profit was T$1.864 billion against T$2.559 billion in May, reflecting higher-than-expected crude costs.
The June figures brought the company's accumulated budget deficit to T$15.779 billion for the fiscal year ended June 30, Chinese Petroleum officals said.
"Chinese Petroleum posted a smaller June pre-tax profit due mainly to rising crude import costs during the period," a company official said.
Chinese Petroleum's June oil import costs averaged US$18.66 per barrel, higher than the budgeted US$15.26 and higher than May's actual US$17.76 import cost, company figures showed.
With state approval, Chinese Petroleum raised prices of petroleum products by an average nine percent on January 1 and a further 2.97 percent on April 4.
Executives have said the added revenues were needed, despite a general decline in world crude prices, to cover what had been a rapidly growing accumulated budget deficit.
